questions.question: The population of a town rises by 20% in the first year, falls by 25% in the second, and rises by 10% in the third. If it is 59,400 at the end of three years, what was the initial population?
A sells an article to B at a 20% profit; B sells it to C at a 10% loss; C sells it to D for ₹2,646, making a 22.5% profit. What did A pay for the article, in ₹?

Two runners start together from the same point on a 400 m circular track, running in the same direction at 5 m/s and 3 m/s. After how many seconds do they meet at the starting point for the first time?
questions.solution: The faster runner returns to the start every 80 s, the slower every 400/3 s. LCM(80, 400/3) = LCM(240, 400)/3 = 1200/3 = 400 s.

questions.question: A car covers the first third of a journey at 30 km/h, the second third at 45 km/h and the last third at 90 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey, in km/h?

Pipes A and B fill a tank in 12 and 15 hours; pipe C empties it in 20 hours. All three are opened together at 6 a.m., and C is closed at 10 a.m. At what hour of the day (in 24-hour format, e.g. 15 for 3 p.m.) is the tank full?
questions.solution: Net rate with C = 5/60 + 4/60 − 3/60 = 6/60 = 1/10, so 4 hours fill 2/5. The remaining 3/5 at 9/60 per hour takes 4 hours. The tank is full at 6 + 4 + 4 = 14, i.e. 2 p.m.

questions.question: Two alloys contain gold and copper in the ratios 2 : 3 and 5 : 3. How many kg of the second must be mixed with 10 kg of the first to obtain an alloy with gold and copper in equal amounts?
questions.solution: Gold: 4 + 5x/8; copper: 6 + 3x/8. Setting them equal gives 2x/8 = 2, so x = 8 kg.

questions.question: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 10% per annum is ₹1,550. What is the sum, in ₹?
Let n be the least positive integer such that 180 divides 150ⁿ. If m is the least positive integer such that 150ⁿ divides 180ᵐ, what is m + n?
questions.solution: 180 = 2² × 3² × 5 and 150 = 2 × 3 × 5². Step 1: 150ⁿ = 2ⁿ3ⁿ5²ⁿ needs n ≥ 2 for both 2² and 3², so n = 2. Step 2: 150² = 2² × 3² × 5⁴ must divide 180ᵐ = 2²ᵐ3²ᵐ5ᵐ; the 5s force m ≥ 4, so m = 4. Step 3: m + n = 6.

questions.question: The average of five distinct positive integers is 20 and their median is 22. What is the largest possible value of the largest of them?
questions.solution: The sum is 100. To maximise the largest, minimise the others: 1, 2, 22, 23 total 48, leaving 52.

questions.question: The roots of x² − 6x + k = 0 are α and β, with α² − β² = 24 and α > β. What is k?
questions.solution: α + β = 6 and α² − β² = 24, so α − β = 4. Then α = 5, β = 1 and k = αβ = 5.

questions.question: How many ordered pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfy x² − y² = 2025?
questions.solution: (x − y)(x + y) = 2025 = 3⁴ × 5². Both factors must be odd (they are, since 2025 is odd) with x − y < x + y. 2025 has 15 divisors; excluding 45 × 45 (which gives y = 0), there are 7 pairs with d < 2025/d.

questions.question: x and y are positive reals with x + 2y = 12. What is the maximum possible value of x²y?
questions.solution: Write x + 2y = x/2 + x/2 + 2y. By AM–GM, (x/2)(x/2)(2y) ≤ 4³ = 64, so x²y/2 ≤ 64 and x²y ≤ 128, with equality at x = 8, y = 2.

questions.question: If log₃ x + log₉ x + log₂₇ x = 11/2, what is x?
f(x) = (3x + 2)/(x − 3) for x ≠ 3. What is f(f(f(f(5))))?
questions.solution: f(f(x)) = x for this function: (3f + 2)/(f − 3) = (3(3x+2) + 2(x−3))/((3x+2) − 3(x−3)) = 11x/11 = x. So applying f four times returns 5.

questions.question: How many terms are common to the arithmetic progressions 4, 9, 14, …, 499 and 3, 10, 17, …, 500?
questions.solution: Common terms form an AP with difference 35. The first common term is 24 (24 = 4 + 20 = 3 + 21). The terms 24, 59, …, up to 499 number ⌊(499 − 24)/35⌋ + 1 = 13 + 1 = 14.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB = 13, BC = 14 and CA = 15. If m is the length of the median from A to BC, what is m²?
questions.solution: By Apollonius' theorem, m² = (2b² + 2c² − a²)/4 = (450 + 338 − 196)/4 = 148.

questions.question: A ladder 25 m long leans against a vertical wall with its foot 7 m from the wall. If the top slides down 4 m, how far, in m, does the foot slide outward?
questions.solution: The original height is 24 m; the new height is 20 m. The new distance is √(625 − 400) = 15, so the foot slides 15 − 7 = 8 m.

questions.question: A rectangular sheet 44 cm × 18 cm is rolled along its longer side to form a hollow cylinder of height 18 cm. What is the volume of the cylinder, in cm³? (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.solution: Circumference 44 = 2πr gives r = 7. Volume = (22/7) × 49 × 18 = 2772.

questions.question: What are the last two digits of 3^2026?
How many positive integers less than 500 have exactly three positive divisors?
questions.solution: Exactly three divisors means n = p² for a prime p. p² < 500 needs p ≤ 22: p = 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. That is 8 numbers.

questions.question: In how many ways can 12 identical chocolates be distributed among 4 children so that each child gets at least 2 and no child gets more than 5?
questions.solution: With yᵢ = xᵢ − 2, we need y₁ + … + y₄ = 4 with each yᵢ ≤ 3. Unrestricted: C(7,3) = 35. Subtract the 4 cases where one yᵢ = 4: 35 − 4 = 31.

questions.question: A bag holds 4 red and 6 blue balls. Balls are drawn one at a time, without replacement, until both colours have appeared. What is the expected number of draws?
questions.solution: Let D be the number of draws. D > k exactly when the first k balls are all one colour. Step 1: E[D] = Σₖ≥0 P(D > k) = 1 + Σₖ≥1 [P(first k all red) + P(first k all blue)]. Step 2: P(first k red) = C(4,k)/C(10,k) and P(first k blue) = C(6,k)/C(10,k). Step 3: red terms 4/10 + 6/45 + 4/120 + 1/210 = 0.5714…; blue terms 6/10 + 15/45 + 20/120 + 15/210 + 6/252 + 1/210 = 1.2. Step 4: E[D] = 1 + 0.5714… + 1.2 = 2.7714… = 97/35.
